articles.title: 'I'm interested in governance, not politics': Leander Paes on AITA presidency bid
articles.summary: Tennis News: It was in the summer of 1996 that Leander Paes won a historic medal at the Atlanta Olympics, ending India’s 44-year wait for an individual Olympic med.
articles.body: It was in the summer of 1996 that Leander Paes won a historic medal at the Atlanta Olympics, ending India’s 44-year wait for an individual Olympic medal. Paes, then 23, battled through a wrist injury, coming back from a set down to beat Brazil’s Fernando Meligeni in the bronze-medal play-off clash.That day, Aug 3, 1996, the effervescent Kolkatan wrote himself into history, providing the punctuation that ended India’s dismal streak at the quadrennial Games.Thirty years later, he is looking to deliver another winner. As he runs for the office of president of the All India Tennis Association, elections for which is stated to be held later this year, Paes wants to turn around a sports body that has been in the news for playing truant.In New York for the US Open, he spoke to TOI about his plans and goals for Indian tennis.Excerpts...When did you decide to run for AITA presidency?I was always interested in a conversation looking at the betterment of Indian tennis, focussing on greater access for players, access to tournaments and professional coaching, building grassroots programs, infrastructure development across states. I’ve given serious thought to reciprocal programs, using my profile and identity across the tennis world, to give our players exposure to coaching systems in countries that have already done the groundwork.What got me thinking was noticing a certain trend, if you can call it that, over the last 15-20 years. It was our tradition of winning Grand Slams, four of us have won Grand Slams in India — Sania (Mirza), Mahesh (Bhupathi), Rohan (Bopanna) and myself. Between us India has won 38 Grand Slam titles, and also held the No.1 ranking in doubles. Besides, Somdev Devvarman, Sania and now Sumit Nagal is doing inspirational stuff in singles, giving us great results at the Tour-level, Olympics, Davis and Billie Jean King cups, but as I see it, in the last couple of decades, there hasn’t been a maximisation of these results.We have had success, so I ask, what did we do with it? Did we capitalise on it? I feel strongly that the players have not been supported, not those who achieved the results nor those who are trying to forge career paths now.Why did you throw yourself in the race?Over the years, in the last decade or so, I have been approached by different people, be it players, well-wishers of Indian tennis or office bearers of state associations, coming up to me and saying, why don't you do something for tennis in India? What has been talked about the most is financial transparency, or sadly, the complete lack of it.While I was playing tennis, I was focussed on my career. Most of the last eight years have gone in looking after my parents, who have both passed away in the last one year. Something like this needs time, needs personal investment.So, besides wanting to bring in a professional system to tennis, grassroot programs, access to all, a clear and clean development pathway, and all of this done with transparency, where everything is open and known to all, I want to put players at the heart of tennis. At the end of the day, results speak louder than anything else.I’m happy to use my personal equity, my name, in attracting corporate and government investment to take this dream of all tennis lovers forward.Did you ever speak to your dad, Dr Vece Paes, about running tennis in the country?Dad and I have had many conversations about governance of sport in India, especially AITA. Every time we had these conversations, he would say, you are in a tough position. His argument was, if you don't take that position, how can you make a difference? But if you do take the position, all your friends, all those who respect and love you for all that you achieved and stood by, will wonder… Also, the minute you take that position, all that you achieved may take a back seat and all the trophies and medals you have worked hard to win may cease to matter because this is a different race, and you might ask yourself, to what end?But, he always said, if you get in, you have to run it as a professional, just like the way you played the sport. Most importantly, you've got to bring the best team together, and you've got to involve the players.You have to make AITA a professional organization, you have to start by professionalizing it, state by state. To help the game grow, getting hands on involved in the development is not an option.I have so much respect for all our fellow players who struggled, worked hard, and spent their own or family money to stay on tour, pay for their hotel, pay for flights, pay for coaching. Some of them travel with companions or partners, but most of our singles and doubles players are doing all this with zero support.What is your vision for tennis in India for the next 10 years?I’m looking at rounded growth while laying out a business plan for tennis. The sport is played round the year, well almost, globally. I want India to have a full calendar too, men, women and juniors. In the last 10-15 years, we in Asia, and those in the global fraternity, have seen what China has done. In Europe you have seen what Italy, Spain and France have done. We need to have tournaments for players. That’s the ground rule, they shouldn’t have to travel abroad for the bulk of their points.At the end of the day, we are in a system where ranking is king, depending on their ranking a player gets into tournaments, that’s their livelihood. For someone playing World Tennis (ITF) junior events, it is like going to school, exposure at every grade of competition is mandatory, it is the foundation they lay for when they turn pro. I want to focus on a tournament structure that allows players to play a bulk of their tournaments at home, and some in Asia where it is easier to travel. This at the developmental stage, once a player has points, it is easier to get into main draws.The goal is to get approximately 15 singles players into Grand Slams – men and women, get multiple teams into the Grand Slam doubles and mixed doubles.Look at China today, 20 years ago people were saying China is building these tennis schools, all these great stadiums across the country, China is looking at investing millions and millions of dollars into player development, in getting international coaching. I look at the US Open draw now and I see Chinese players across the board. A lot of work has already been done.The other goal I have is to get the administration of AITA to such a level that it sets the standard for other sports associations in the country. I want our past players to get involved in different levels of the game, for example coaching, like Sania and Rohan are already doing. Sport and event management like Mahesh and Vijay have dabbled with, and I have dabbled with.Even get the current players involved, so when we are done we can hand it over to the next generation. There has to be investment by the past, present, and future players, just like there has to be investment by corporate India and investment by the government.How do you plan to go about getting the players together?We begin by having conversations, the players need to come together and work together, this is our sport, we must take ownership of it. Just because we have had differences of opinion, or people live in different countries that doesn’t mean he or she is forgotten. We have to find a way to work together and I’m willing to lead the way, I’m interested in governance, not politics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Zverev quiere la Copa Davis este año: juega y gana para Alemania
articles.standfirst: El flamante campeón del US Open ha jugado este sábado en Halle seis días después de la consecución del US Open
articles.summary: El flamante campeón del US Open ha jugado este sábado en Halle seis días después de la consecución del US Open
articles.body: La Copa Davis no es lo que era, pero sigue atrayendo a las mejores raquetas del mundo, algunas, como Alexander Zverev, huérfanas de la máxima competición por países. Eso contrasta con la espantada anual en la fase final de la Billie Jean King Cup. Mientras Zverev jugó y ganó este sábado representando a Alemania seis días después de llevarse el US Open —el finalista Ben Shelton defiende desde el viernes a Estados Unidos en la República Checa—, la kazaja Elena Rybakina se ha borrado sin más de la serie con España del próximo miércoles en la ciudad china de Shenzhen. Tampoco están Paula Badosa, Emma Raducanu... A Rybakina, la nueva número uno mundial y campeona del Abierto neoyorquino, parece no motivarle jugar por Kazajistán y adjudicarse la BJK Cup. Zverev y Shelton están haciendo un acto de patriotismo el fin de semana para intentar clasificar a sus respectivos países para la Final a 8 de Bolonia. Sascha ha puesto la primera piedra en la serie con Croacia de Halle al derrotar a Matej Dodig, el 171 de la ATP, por 6-4 y 7-6(3). Al tenista natural de Hamburgo, de 29 años, le falta la Copa Davis en un palmarés donde ya aparece todo lo demás: Grand Slam, Masters 1000, ATP Finals, medalla de oro olímpica y torneos de categoría 500 y 250. Es consciente de que este puede ser el año porque su equipo es de los más compensados, con un doble de garantías como el que forman Kevin Krawietz y Tim Puetz, flamantes finalistas en el grande neoyorquino. Ellos también dejaron el jet lag a un lado para intentar hacerse con uno de los siete billetes en juego para la fase final. Daniel Altmaier, la segunda raqueta alemana, falló en el intento de anotare el 2-0. Su verdugo fue Dino Prizmic, por 6-4 y 6-3. La derrota de Altmaier obliga a Zverev ha hacer un sobreesfuerzo y tener que saltar también el domingo.

articles.body:
Última hora del Tabilo - Mérida, en directo

Buenas tardes, bienvenidos al primer día de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis ante Chile. Hoy tendremos en pista a los guerreros que intentarán firmar los dos primeros puntos y encarrilar el pase a la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24-29 de noviembre). Para hacer un breve repaso, Rafa Jódar, Dani Mérida, Jaume Munar, Martín Landaluce y Pedro Martínez, son los seleccionados por David Ferrer para la batalla sobre la tierra de Chile. Por el combinado local, Alejandro Tabilo, Cristian Garín, Tomás Barrios Vera, Matías Soto y Benjamín Pérez lucharán bajo las órdenes de Nicolás Massú, por mantener la racha de 15 años sin ceder en una eliminatoria de Copa Davis como anfitriones. Hoy se disputarán los dos primeros encuentros de individuales. Dani Mérida y Alejandro Tabilo abrirán la eliminatoria a la 13:00 h en horario chileno.

Dani Mérida viene en su mejor momento como tenista profesional. Marca el puesto 41 en el ranking ATP y viene de completar una más que notable gira americana de pista dura firmando los cuartos de final en el Masters 1000 de Montreal. Lo de hoy, es una historia completamente distinta. La Court Central Anita Lizana apretará más que nunca por ver a los suyos en Bolonia, y los chilenos en tierra... no son muy de fiar. A continuación de lo que haga Mérida, saltará a pista otro madrileño debutante en esta edición, Rafa Jódar, que buscará el primer o segundo punto para el equipo español.

articles.title: Davis Cup 2026: Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery give Great Britain 2-0 lead over Ecuador
articles.summary: Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery get Britain off to a winning start in their Davis Cup qualifying tie against Ecuador.
articles.body:
Toby Samuel says he was "caught off guard" about how much his Davis Cup debut meant to him as he got Great Britain off to a winning start in their qualifying tie against Ecuador.

The 24-year-old overcame nerves to fight back from a set down against Andres Andrade and put the hosts in front at London's sold-out Copper Box Arena.

Team-mate Arthur Fery, playing on home soil for the first time since his astonishing run to the Wimbledon semi-finals, then gave Britain a 2-0 lead with a commanding 7-5 6-0 win over Alvaro Guillen Meza.

"It's a completely new experience for me playing Davis Cup and it definitely caught me off guard how much it meant to me going out there for my first time," Samuel, who has enjoyed a breakthrough 2026 season, told BBC Sport.

"It almost felt like a bigger deal than playing any Slam for me."

Samuel has made his debut at three Grand Slams and climbed from outside of the world's top 250 to 95th in the men's singles rankings in the past nine months.

He was only handed his chance to play in the Davis Cup on Friday after British number two Cameron Norrie pulled out of the tie with an arm injury.

His debut got off to a tricky start as Andrade, ranked 203rd in the world, won the opening four games without reply en route to taking the first set 6-4.

But Samuel recovered to successfully navigate a tight second set before storming through the decider in 28 minutes, dropping just one game to wrap up a 4-6 6-4 6-1 win.

"This was a big dream of mine and you could sort of tell because I got a bit nervous at the start, but I got myself going and I am so happy I got the job done for Great Britain," he said in his on-court interview.

As Samuel made his way courtside to watch along with the raucous crowd, Fery made his first appearance for his country as the British number one.

Fery, who has risen to 36th in the world following his run to the last four at Wimbledon and the final at Winston-Salem, was forced to work hard in an enthralling hour-long opening set.

However, his quality soon shone through and he won eight games in a row to sweep aside world number 293 Guillen Meza.

"We're used to travelling alone the whole year and coming out as a team in front of all you of you guys today in London is unbelievable," Fery said to the crowd.

"The tennis schedule is pretty relentless and we are playing week after week so you have to keep that motivation high, but it's easy to keep that motivation when you are playing for your country and representing the GB colours in front of everyone here with a team like this."

Henry Patten and Neal Skupski can wrap up the best-of-five tie at the earliest opportunity if they triumph in Sunday's doubles from 12:00 BST.

If not, Fery and Samuel will have to return to the court for the reverse singles to try and secure Britain's place in the knockout stage for the first time since 2023.

The seven winners of this weekend's qualifying ties will join three-time defending champions Italy in the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna from 24 to 29 November.

Austria and South Korea booked their tickets to the quarter-finals on Saturday with victories over Belgium and India respectively.

The United States, who have won the competition a record 32 times, lead the Czech Republic 2-1, while Canada are 2-0 up against France.

articles.title: The ‘broken system’ in tennis Andy Roddick complained about 15 years ago that still hasn’t been fixed
articles.summary: Any casual tennis fan might be under the impression that the season ends following the US Open and begins once again when the Australian Open...
articles.body:
Any casual tennis fan might be under the impression that the season ends following the US Open and begins once again when the Australian Open rolls around in the New Year.

While pretty much every other sport on the planet offers its players long off-seasons to properly rest their bodies and take time to heal from any nagging injuries, tennis just keeps going; pretty much all year round.

There is about a month and a half between the final event of the year, the ATP Finals, and the first tournament of the following season.

For the top players, the tennis schedule can be absolutely brutal, as deep runs at tournaments mean even less time off before the next one starts.

The issue around the packed calendar is not a new one, and in 2011, Andy Roddick used the term 'broken system' to describe the problem that still persists today.

What Andy Roddick said about the tennis schedule back in 2011

After winning his opening match at the Shanghai Masters that year, Roddick was asked about Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer, who were no-shows at the ATP 1000 tournament.

"My views are pretty clear on it," began the former US Open champion. "You know, people have to understand, people act like we pull out and we get something out of it.

"We don't get anything. They're out of the bonus pool now. They don't get their money this week. I'm sure there's something in their contract somewhere. It benefits them to be there.

"Obviously, if they were feeling well and they weren't worn down, then they would. We're not getting away with anything by pulling out of tournaments. I feel like that's the way it's presented sometimes. That's just not the case."

At the US Open earlier that season, there was a lot of talk about players meeting at the Shanghai Masters to discuss the scheduling issues.

By the time the Shanghai Masters came around, it felt as though momentum around the discussions had died down, but Roddick confirmed: "The sentiment is still there.

He said: "I think it is a broken system purely from a numbers game on votes on our, you know, player board and council and all that. As long as we're one vote short, nothing's really going to happen. I think the inherent issues that we're facing are still there.

"You know, I hope guys are as passionate as they were. But, as I said, I'm one of the only ones who played today.

"From what I've been reading, there are still some issues. You know, so we'll see. I mean, I think it would be dumb of us to rush anything. If something like this does happen, we need to be smart about it and take our time and make sure that it's well thought out and not be kind of reactionary."

Andy Roddick's issue with the end section of the tennis season

Asked what other things about the tour he would like to see fixed other than the scheduling, Roddick replied: "Well, that's a major issue.

"I said last week in Beijing, that was an issue when I started in '01 or '02, I remember in Bercy (The Paris Masters).

"But I also remember in Bercy it being the last event of the year, and I would celebrate Halloween there.

"Now it's mid-November. It's November 14th that Bercy finishes. So with all the talk, it's actually gotten longer, and that's if you don't make Masters.

"So the guys that play the most are playing into early December, some of them, for Davis Cup. Obviously, that's not the direction that you want to see. So that's a major issue.

"You know, if we're getting selfish about it, I think players get 13% of total revenue, something like that, from the US Open, and the NBA is at a crossroads because they're going to have to go from 57% to 50%. That's an alarming number.

"That's not the be all, end all. I think we all feel very fortunate for what we get, but we are putting people in seats."

For those who don't make the ATP Finals, the last big tournament of the year is the Paris Masters, which, this year, ends on the eighth of November.

articles.title: Butler athletics announces upgrades to tennis and volleyball programs
articles.summary: Butler athletics announced projects that will provide significant upgrades to the tennis and volleyball programs.
articles.body:
Butler Athletics announced two projects that will provide significant upgrades to the tennis and volleyball programs.

Butler has begun construction on a multi-million dollar, 12-court outdoor tennis facility. The facility will include fencing, spectator seating areas, scoreboard and other amenities. The project was made possible through donations and a grant from the United State Tennis Association.

"We are excited to get underway on this project," Butler Vice President and Director of Athletics Grant Leiendecker said of the new tennis facility. "This facility will provide our Butler tennis programs and student-athletes with a home to train, compete, and represent The Butler Way.

"This facility will also serve the Central Indiana tennis community and bring countless visitors to our campus every year. We can't thank our donors enough for their incredible investment in this project, and we look forward to hosting matches soon."

See photos from Butler Bulldog men's basketball practice

Inside Hinkle Fieldhouse, the Butler volleyball team kicked off the Butler Invitational by debuting its new Taraflex floor. The Taraflex flooring goes over the Hinkle Fieldhouse court, providing increased shock absorption which reduces the force on the player's bodies, lowering the risk of long-term injury. Butler fell to Duke 1-3.

The Taraflex court was provided by a group of donors, led by Nancy and Dr. Dennis Lawton. The Lawtons have a long family history at Butler that dates to 1941 when Nancy's mother, Doris, graduated from Butler. In her honor, the couple established the Doris Huesing Barrett and Dennis and Nancy H. Lawton Endowed Fund for Men's Basketball in 2010. The fund provides support for the team's area of greatest need as determined by the head coach.In 2014, the couple established the Lawton Family Scholarship for Men's Basketball, which is awarded annually to a scholarship athlete. In 2019, the strength and conditioning room in Hinkle Fieldhouse was named for the family.

"A Taraflex court has been a goal for our program over the last few years as we have prioritized ways to elevate Butler volleyball," Butler volleyball coach Kyle Shondell said. "So many shared our vision and have generously supported this initiative, spearheaded by Nancy and Denny. When we surprised the team with our new court, it was amazing for Nancy and Denny to be there with us and to experience the true joy and appreciation from our team. We are proud that the Lawton Family name will be on the Butler volleyball court for years to come."

articles.title: Davis Cup: Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel give Great Britain lead over Ecuador to move them closer to knockout stage
articles.summary: Great Britain are one win away from Davis Cup Final 8 after taking 2-0 lead over Ecuador on day one; GB have not reached knockout stage since 2023
articles.body:
Samuel beat Andres Andrade 4-6 6-4 6-1 in the opening match before Wimbledon semi-finalist Fery defeated Alvaro Guillen Meza 7-5 6-0.

Great Britain are now one win away from the Davis Cup Final 8.

On Sunday, Great Britain duo Henry Patten and Neal Skupski will take on Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles where they could secure their passage into the knockout stage for the first time since 2023.

On the eve of the tie Cameron Norrie, their only remaining experienced singles player in the absence of Jack Draper, was ruled out with an arm injury.

Fery had marked his debut in the competition a year ago with victory over Poland's Olaf Pieczkowski.

He is now ranked 36th and followed up his brilliant run to the last four at Wimbledon as a wild card by reaching his first ATP Tour final in the US last month.

Following the win, Fery said: "It was awesome. You get goosebumps walking out. It was great playing here, obviously in London, a lot of support from everyone.

"It's always different playing Davis Cup. You're playing for a whole nation, there's more responsibility on your shoulders. It's a weight that I can carry and I felt confident out there."

Samuel, who lost the opening four games before clawing back against Ecuador's number one, said: "That's definitely the most nerves I've had before a match, even more than the slams I've played.

"I obviously didn't start off as good as I wanted to and I went down, but I was like, 'you're a good player, I keep playing my game and I keep believing and get myself going a bit and it will come', and it did in the end.

"It's even better than I thought. The feeling you get when you get the win for your country is something I've never felt like I've experienced before."

Germany are currently level with Croatia at 1-1, Austria lead Belgium 3-1, South Korea lead India by the same scoreline, while Canada lead France 2-0. Spain lead Chile 2-0.

articles.title: Mérida ha nacido para jugar la Copa Davis y da el primer punto ante Tabilo
articles.standfirst: El madrileño remonta un set con la tranquilidad de un veterano y adelanta a España en la serie en tierras chilenas
articles.summary: El madrileño remonta un set con la tranquilidad de un veterano y adelanta a España en la serie en tierras chilenas
articles.body: Hay jugadores que han nacido para jugar la Copa Davis y otros que no. En el primer grupo está encima de la lista Dani Mérida, que ha puesto la primera piedra hacia Bolonia ganando este sábado a Alejandro Tabilo, por 5-7, 6-3 y 6-3. En el recuerdo, la victoria de Félix Mantilla en Nueva Zelanda, en el playoff de 1999, cuando también debutó en el torneo junto a Pato Clavet. Tabilo, de 29 años y en el puesto 28 del ranking, con 16 eliminatorias de Davis a sus espaldas, ha hincado la rodilla este sábado en el primer punto del playoff ante España clasificatorio para la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). El número uno chileno, apoyado desde la primera fila por otro zurdo célebre como Marcelo Ríos, se ha visto impotente ante la remontada de un Mérida que en su debut en la máxima competición por países ha enseñado todas las armas que le han convertido en una de las revelaciones del presente curso. Dani lo hizo todo bien y sólo un break en contra en el undécimo asalto le costó la manga inicial. Desde entonces, se puso a devolverlo todo. Para algo es el mejor restador del circuito masculino. Mérida se fue a la silla de cambios con la sensación de haber sufrido demasiado castigo. Escuchaba atentamente las indicaciones del capitán, David Ferrer. Le tocaba remontar en tierra hostil. Cada vez se hacían más evidentes los gritos de la grada cuando fallaba el primer servicio. Con frío (la temperatura era de 16 grados) y la dificultad de jugar en polvo de ladrillo y a 520 metros de altura, condiciones distintas respecto al reciente US Open, el madrileño se sobrepuso como un grande. Rafa Jódar debutará ahora con Cristian Garín con el alivio de saber que España va por delante en el marcador. La selección está un paso más cerca de repetir en Bolonia. Chile no ha perdido de local en 15 años (italia fue su último verdugo en 2011) y Nicolás Massú suma 12 eliminatorias ganadas en su casa desde que se sentó por primera vez en el banquillo en 2014. Esa racha está un poco más cerca de romperse gracias a la 'Armada' nacional.

articles.title: Garín - Jódar: resultado, resumen y estadísticas de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis
articles.summary: Lo dejamos por aquí hoy. Disponible la crónica del partido en MARCA. Seguro que seguiremos teniendo grandes noticias del equipo español en el futuro.
articles.body:
Última hora del Garín - Jódar, en directo

Buenas tardes, bienvenidos al primer día de la eliminatoria de Copa Davis ante Chile. Hoy tendremos en pista a los guerreros que intentarán firmar los dos primeros puntos y encarrilar el pase a la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24-29 de noviembre). Para hacer un breve repaso, Rafa Jódar, Dani Mérida, Jaume Munar, Martín Landaluce y Pedro Martínez, son los seleccionados por David Ferrer para la batalla sobre la tierra de Chile. Por el combinado local, Alejandro Tabilo, Cristian Garín, Tomás Barrios Vera, Matías Soto y Benjamín Pérez lucharán bajo las órdenes de Nicolas Massú, por mantener la racha de 15 años sin ceder en una eliminatoria de Copa Davis como anfitriones. Hoy se disputarán los dos primeros encuentros de individuales. Dani Mérida acaba de ganar a Alejandro Tabilo y brindar el primer punto de la eliminatoria para España. A continuación, saltará a pista el número 1 español en Chile, RAFA JÓDAR ante Cristian Garín.

Rafa Jódar, a pesar de la eliminación en primera ronda del US Open, llega tras una gran primera gira americana de pista dura. Firmó la final en Washington, semifinales en Montreal y octavos en Cincinnati. Hoy, ante Cristian Garín tendrá la opción de poner el 2-0 el marcador y dejar la eliminatoria a un paso de clasificar a la Final a 8 de Bolonia.

articles.title: Kaitlin Quevedo escribe su historia y jugará su primera final en Sao Paulo
articles.standfirst: La tenista española derrotó en tres sets a la rusa Blinkova y este lunes tendrá su mejor ranking como profesional
articles.summary: La tenista española derrotó en tres sets a la rusa Blinkova y este lunes tendrá su mejor ranking como profesional
articles.body: Kaitlin Quevedo será la última española en incorporarse a la concentración de la selección española de la Billie Jean King Cup que buscará, desde el próximo miércoles 24, el cetro de la máxima competición por países. Tiene una buena excusa para ello porque Quevedo se ha clasificado este sábado para su primera final WTA. En el torneo de categoría 250 de Sao Paulo (Brasil), Quevedo ha tumbado en tres sets a la rusa Anna Blinkova, cuarta cabeza de serie del cuadro, por 6-4, 2-6 y 6-4. Kaitlin, que empezó la semana fuera del 'top100', se ha asegurado ya el puesto 91, el mejor de su carrera como profesional. En la lucha por la corona espera a la ganadora de la segunda semifinal que enfrentará a su compatriota Paula Badosa y la argentina Nadia Podoroska.

articles.title: Jódar acerca a España a las finales cediendo dos juegos ante Garín
articles.standfirst: Rafa no encuentra rival en el chileno y anota el segundo punto de la serie en tierras chilenas
articles.summary: Rafa no encuentra rival en el chileno y anota el segundo punto de la serie en tierras chilenas
articles.body: En la antigua Copa Davis el ranking era lo de menos en las confrontaciones. Toda sorpresa era posible. Es lo que se denominaba la magia de la Davis. En el formato actual se nota y mucho la diferencia de potencial. Chile sólo tiene un 'top100' y se notó en la primera jornada del 'playoff' ante España. Dani Mérida, primero ante Alejandro Tabilo, y Rafa Jódar, después con Cristian Garín, con un 6-0 y 6-2, dieron los dos primeros puntos que acercan a la selección a la Final a 8 de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Garín, el 133 del mundo, demostró su actual clasificación ante un verdugo como Jódar que dejó atrás, con tenis de primer nivel, el reciente traspié en el estreno del US Open con el chino Bu. El Parque Deportivo Estadio Nacional, que apuntaba a caldera, resultó ser un balneario para la dupla de jóvenes elegida por el capitán David Ferrer. Ellos dos, junto a Carlos Alcaraz y Martín Landaluce, aseguran el presente y el futuro de la Armada nacional. Jódar, con los 20 años recién cumplidos, tiene como una de sus principales cualidades que no especula con el resultado. Le hubiera gustado que lo hiciera Garín, que se llevó un rosco en la manga inicial. El madrileño sumó 25 puntos por 10 del rival y llegó a encadenar los primeros siete juegos. Su ritmo de bola era inalcanzable para un adversario que apuntaba mucho cuando se adjudicó el júnior de Roland Garros , en 2013. Se quedó en el camino. La exhibición del tenista de Chamartín acabó con un ganador de revés y tan sólo 17 errores no forzados. Dani y Rafa repiten el debut victorioso que firmaron Félix Mantilla y Francisco Clavet en el cruce en Nueva Zelanda de 1999. Jaume Munar y Pedro Martínez se juntarán por tercera vez este domingo en la máxima competición por países. Se mantienen invictos tras debutar la pasada campaña en tierras suizas y ganar al dúo formado por Huesler y Stricker. Posteriormente, superaron en la tierra de Marbella a Holmgren e Ingildsen. Ahora toca Tabilo y Barrios.

articles.title: Lehecka deja sin Copa Davis a Estados Unidos por segundo año consecutivo
articles.standfirst: El checo vence a Learner Tien en el partido decisivo y estarán en la Final a 8 de Bolonia
articles.summary: El checo vence a Learner Tien en el partido decisivo y estarán en la Final a 8 de Bolonia
articles.body: República Checa pone rumbo a la Final a 8 de Bolonia (25-29 de noviembre) de la mano de Jiri Lehecka. El cañonero checo ejerció de verdugo del joven americano Learner Tien en el partido decisivo por 6-3 y 7-5. Las 32 ensaladeras de los americanos parecen cosa del pasado. Actúan de máximo ganador pero desde 2007 no consiguen levantar la competición internacional. Este año, al igual que el pasado, han caído en la segunda ronda de la fase clasificatoria ante República Checa. Se hizo notar el ambiente en Praga. Tras el 1-2 inicial favorable a los americanos, Jakub Mensik y Jiri Lehecka tomaron los mandos del país. El primero, encarriló la remontada venciendo a Ben Shelton, finalista del US Open hace seis días, con remontada incluida en tres sets (5-7, 6-4 y 6-3). Esto dejaba la eliminatoria en las manos de Jiri Lehecka y Learner Tien. Pero el checo, actual número 24 del mundo, mostró sus galones desde el principio. Un 'break' decisivo con 4-3 en el marcador, le sirvió para sacar y llevarse la primera manga. En la segunda, tuvo que empelarse a fondo ya que el californiano llegó a liderar por 0-3. Recuperó, y otra rotura en el tramo final para colocarse 6-5 y saque acabó con los nervios en Praga. República Checa disputará la Final a 8 en Bolonia. Hasta el momento, los equipos clasificados son: Italia, como campeón del año pasado, Corea del Sur, Austria y República Checa.

articles.title: La fábrica de campeones de Feliciano López y ESS abre su segundo curso en Madrid
articles.standfirst: La ESS Feli López Academy estrena temporada en el Tejar de Somontes con residencia, calendario propio de torneos y un atractivo programa académico que otorga el High School Diploma, dentro de una oferta de ESS que abarca también baloncesto, fútbol, golf y pádel bajo el modelo de carrera dual
articles.summary: La ESS Feli López Academy estrena temporada en el Tejar de Somontes con residencia, calendario propio de torneos y un atractivo programa académico que otorga el High School Diploma, dentro de una oferta de ESS que abarca también baloncesto, fútbol, golf y pádel bajo el modelo de carrera dual
articles.body: Feliciano López volvió esta semana a ejercer de anfitrión en Madrid. El extenista, de la mano de European School of Sports (ESS), presentó la segunda temporada de la ESS Feli López Academy, el proyecto que combina tenis de alto rendimiento y formación académica reglada. Un año después de su estreno, la academia cambia de sede, ensancha su oferta y afianza una idea pionera en España: preparar tenistas sin obligarles a elegir entre la pista y el aula. El programa se ha instalado en las instalaciones del Tejar de Somontes, donde el alumnado dispone de residencia, pensión completa, traslados diarios y un calendario personalizado de torneos. La academia se presenta como la primera iniciativa de estas características en la capital y una de las pocas en Europa que compagina de manera real el trabajo diario en pista con una titulación académica homologada. Las inscripciones siguen abiertas para jugadores con proyección nacional e internacional. Feliciano López no firma el proyecto desde la distancia. El extenista dirige personalmente la academia y ejerce como figura tutelar, con presencia habitual en entrenamientos y actividades con las familias. "El deporte y la educación deben ir siempre unidos de la mano. Madrid vive un gran momento y debemos aprovechar la oportunidad para ofrecer lo mejor a estos chicos", subrayó durante la presentación. Su implicación, más allá del reclamo comercial, se ha convertido en una seña de identidad del programa. Al frente del área deportiva figura Carlos Castillo, técnico con más de tres décadas de recorrido en el tenis de alto rendimiento. Castillo formó parte del cuerpo técnico de la Federación de Tenis de Madrid y ha trabajado con jugadores del calibre de Virginia Ruano, múltiple campeona de Grand Slam y doble medallista olímpica. Su metodología, apoyada en un equipo multidisciplinar, atiende la técnica, la táctica, la preparación física, la nutricional y la mental de cada alumno de la casa. La pata académica se sostiene sobre el sistema educativo estadounidense y permite a los estudiantes-deportistas obtener el High School Diploma. Las clases se concentran por la tarde para respetar los ritmos de entrenamiento, y cada alumno cuenta con un tutor personalizado que le acompaña durante todo el itinerario. El modelo abre puertas a las becas universitarias en Estados Unidos y contempla también la continuidad de los estudios en España o en otras universidades internacionales. ESS ha reforzado la temporada con un programa propio de becas destinado a captar a los mayores talentos, previa evaluación de la candidatura. "Queremos atraer a deportistas internacionales que vengan a España a desarrollarse y a seguir con su formación académica. Creemos que España puede ser un hub de formación de deportistas de cualquier disciplina", explicó Carlos López, consejero delegado y fundador de la institución. La ambición del proyecto, por tanto, cruza fronteras desde el mismo arranque del segundo curso. European School of Sports, respaldada por empresarios como Jon Uriarte y Kike Levy, complementa su oferta con programas específicos de baloncesto, fútbol, golf y pádel, entre otras disciplinas. La ESS Feli López Academy funciona así como buque insignia de un ecosistema más amplio, orientado a la carrera dual y al acompañamiento a largo plazo de los jóvenes deportistas. La segunda temporada arranca con el listón alto y con la promesa de que Madrid ya tiene un actor nuevo en la formación tenística de élite.
